Features.lead: Five modules that work together. Here's what each one does.

focus.lead: Work sessions with a single goal.
focus.p1: Pick the task that matters and start a timer.
focus.p2: Pause and resume without losing your thread.
focus.p3: A sound tells you when you pause and when the session is done.

tasks.p1: High, medium or low priority on every task.

About.title: About us
About.lead: Nexus Life is an independent project born from a simple idea: organizing your day shouldn't take five different apps.
About.body: We're building it step by step and learning along the way: a React Native mobile app and this Next.js website, with the care of a real product.

Tech.title: Built with modern technology
Tech.lead: A personal project with product standards: layered architecture, automated tests and two languages.

app.title: The mobile app
app.text: Built with React Native and Expo, styled with NativeWind, state managed with Zustand, and a clean architecture split into modules.

web.title: This website
web.text: Next.js with server rendering, TypeScript, Tailwind, GSAP animations and next-intl translations.

assistant.title: The assistant
assistant.text: A Telegram bot with layered logic, data in Upstash Redis and a free Groq AI model as a fallback.

Privacy.title: Privacy and data
Privacy.lead: What each part of the project does with your information, explained without fine print.

web.title: This website
web.text: We don't include analytics or tracking cookies. Only your theme and language preferences are stored in your browser. The hosting provider (Vercel) may log technical data about visits.

bot.title: Assistant (Telegram and web chat)
bot.text: On Telegram it answers with predefined texts and, if it can't find an answer, queries a free AI model (Groq). In the web chat, your latest messages are sent to Groq to generate the reply. We don't store those conversations. The chat limits messages per visitor (by IP, only for a few minutes) to prevent abuse.

app.title: The app
app.text: It's still in development, so its privacy policy isn't published yet.
